sources.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (December 1997), 238 PDF pages
sources.locator: Ch. 1 'Special Relativity and Flat Spacetime' printed pp. 4-9 (PDF pp. 11-16): the metric, x^0 = ct, energy-momentum; Ch. 2 'Manifolds' printed pp. 44-51 (PDF pp. 51-58): vectors as derivatives, coordinate bases, the tensor transformation law, the metric again, canonical form of the metric; Ch. 3 'Curvature' printed pp. 56-61 (PDF pp. 63-68): covariant derivatives and connections, torsion (3.16), metric compatibility, the Christoffel connection (3.19)-(3.21); Ch. 4 'Gravitation' printed pp. 97-98 and 116-118 (PDF pp. 104-105 and 123-125): physics in curved spacetime, the energy-momentum tensor again, the Weak Energy Condition (4.72).

contents.name: Ch. 2 'vectors as derivatives' and 'coordinate bases' (printed pp. 44-46, PDF pp. 51-53)
contents.support: Tangent vectors are identified with derivations and coordinate bases supply the components used in the definition of a smooth covariant 2-tensor field.

contents.name: Ch. 2 metric transformation law (2.35), printed p. 50 (PDF p. 57)
contents.support: Equation (2.35) supplies the covariant metric transformation template; the general bilinear tensor law is proved locally by the chain rule and bilinearity. Equation (2.26) instead concerns non-tensorial partial derivatives.

contents.name: Ch. 2 'the metric again' and 'canonical form of the metric' (printed pp. 47-50, PDF pp. 54-57)
contents.support: The metric is taken as a smooth symmetric nondegenerate (0,2) tensor field, the inverse metric raises and lowers indices, and the canonical form with one minus sign is the Lorentzian signature condition; the lecture notes' generic-rank warning is replaced by the explicit inertia hypothesis.

contents.name: Ch. 2 'Riemann normal coordinates' and the local flatness discussion (printed pp. 50-51, PDF pp. 57-58)
contents.reason: Point-normal and exponential coordinates belong to the connection and free-fall page, which constructs the metric connection and its normal charts; this page fixes only the geometry and the metric-compatibility conditions.

contents.name: Ch. 3 'covariant derivatives and connections' and 'connection coefficients' (printed pp. 56-59, PDF pp. 63-66)
contents.support: The lecture notes define a connection by its component rule nabla_mu and its transformation, and impose metric compatibility and torsion freedom as the two conditions selecting the connection; the definition here states the two conditions for the already-defined affine connection of the library.

contents.name: Ch. 3 torsion tensor (3.16) and metric compatibility (printed pp. 59-60, PDF pp. 66-67)
contents.support: Torsion is the antisymmetric part of the connection coefficients and metric compatibility is nabla_rho g_{mu nu} = 0; both are restated as the Leibniz identity and the vanishing torsion of the library's torsion definition.

contents.name: Ch. 3 'the Christoffel connection' (3.19)-(3.21) and the polar-coordinate example (printed pp. 60-61, PDF pp. 67-68)
contents.reason: The derivation that a torsion-free compatible connection must have the Christoffel components, and the caution that existence is left to a check, are exactly the selection theorem of the connections page; no uniqueness claim is made on this page.

contents.name: Ch. 4 opening of 'physics in curved spacetime' (printed p. 97, PDF p. 104)
contents.support: The lecture notes 'state the laws governing physics in curved spacetime' by taking a Lorentzian manifold as the arena; the postulate records that adoption and its classical-domain restriction.

contents.name: Ch. 4 'the energy-momentum tensor again' (printed pp. 116-118, PDF pp. 123-125)
contents.support: The energy-momentum tensor is defined as the symmetric tensor appearing on the right side of Einstein's equations, to be specified by the matter model; the definition here fixes the slot, its symmetry and its units without adopting any matter branch.

contents.name: Ch. 4 the Weak Energy Condition (4.72) and the remark that stronger conditions are not treated (printed p. 117, PDF p. 124)
contents.support: The WEC is stated for all timelike vectors and distinguished from stronger conditions; the definition keeps exactly the timelike form and records that the remaining conditions are separate adopted inequalities.

contents.name: Ch. 4 'the Hilbert action' and Einstein's equations (printed pp. 109-115, PDF pp. 116-122)
contents.reason: Deriving the field equations from the Einstein-Hilbert action and defining T by a metric variation is the content of the Einstein-and-matter page, together with the action/direct-equation formulation question.

contents.name: Ch. 1 'energy-momentum tensor', 'perfect fluids' and 'energy-momentum conservation' (printed pp. 6-9, PDF pp. 13-16)
contents.reason: The dust, perfect-fluid and scalar stress-energy branches and the on-shell conservation identity are constructions of the matter page, not part of the geometric arena fixed here.

sources.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), 125 PDF pages; Internet Archive copy of the original Cambridge lecture notes
sources.locator: Conventions PDF p. 1; §1.2-1.8 printed pp. 5-21 (PDF pp. 6-22) on manifolds, curves, covectors, abstract index notation and tensor fields; §2.1-2.2 printed pp. 25-28 (PDF pp. 26-29) on the metric, Lorentzian signature, orthonormal bases, the causal classification and the two disconnected sets of causal vectors; §3.1-3.2 printed pp. 31-37 (PDF pp. 32-38) on the covariant derivative and the Levi-Civita theorem; §6.4 printed p. 67 (PDF p. 68) on the postulates of general relativity.

contents.name: Conventions: units c = 1, abstract indices a,b,c, signature (-+++) (PDF p. 1)
contents.support: The conventions paragraph fixes the signature and natural-unit shorthand that the unit item restates with SI dimensions restored.

contents.name: §1.7-1.8 tensors, outer products and tensor fields, components in a basis (printed pp. 16-21, PDF pp. 17-22)
contents.support: Tensor fields are smooth component families transforming by the Jacobian; the definition specializes this to covariant 2-tensors and proves the chart-independence of the smoothness condition.

contents.name: §2.1 the metric, its inverse and the vector-covector isomorphism (printed pp. 25-27, PDF pp. 26-28)
contents.support: The inverse metric g^{ab}, the identity g^{ab}g_{bc} = delta^a_c and the natural isomorphism X_a = g_{ab}X^b are the definition's pointwise content; smoothness of the components is proved in the companion lemma.

contents.name: §2.2 Lorentzian signature: orthonormal bases at a point, timelike/null/spacelike, causal vectors in two disconnected sets (printed pp. 26-28, PDF pp. 27-29)
contents.support: The classification by the sign of g(X,X), the orthonormal basis existence and the two-component statement are the pointwise inputs; the lemma additionally proves the sign criterion against a timelike field for future and past.

contents.name: §2.2 exercise: a non-zero vector orthogonal to a timelike vector is spacelike (printed p. 27, PDF p. 28)
contents.support: The exercise is the key orthogonality fact; the lemma proves it by the Cauchy-Schwarz bound in an orthonormal basis, and uses it to make the sign of g(v,N) nowhere zero on causal vectors.

contents.name: §2.3 proper time along a timelike curve and curve length (printed pp. 28-30, PDF pp. 29-31)
contents.reason: Proper time is defined on worldlines, whose domain, regularity and clock interpretation are fixed by the free-fall and clock postulates of the connections page; this page defines no curve regularity.

contents.name: §3.1-3.2 the covariant derivative and the Levi-Civita theorem with the Koszul identity (printed pp. 31-37, PDF pp. 32-38)
contents.reason: The existence and uniqueness theorem for the metric connection is stated and proved on the connections page; here only the two conditions and their component forms are fixed, deliberately without asserting the selection theorem.

contents.name: §6.4 postulate 1: spacetime is a 4-dimensional Lorentzian manifold equipped with the Levi-Civita connection (PDF p. 68)
contents.support: The postulate adopts the Lorentzian manifold as the arena of the theory; the spacetime postulate records this adoption with the framework's smooth and classical restrictions.

contents.name: §6.4 postulate 3: energy, momentum and stresses of matter are a symmetric tensor T_ab, conserved (PDF p. 68)
contents.support: The postulate that matter is described by a symmetric tensor is the framework input recorded by the matter postulate; conservation is carried as an on-shell statement of the adopted field law rather than as an automatic property.

contents.name: §6.4 postulates 2 and 4: free particles follow timelike or null geodesics; the Einstein equation relates curvature to T_ab (PDF p. 68)
contents.reason: The geodesic test-body postulate and the field equation belong to the free-fall page and the Einstein-and-matter page respectively, where their exact hypotheses and matter branches are stated.

sources.title: D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), 289 PDF pages; Internet Archive copy of the author-hosted notes
sources.locator: §2.3.3 printed pp. 72-75 (PDF pp. 79-82) on tensors and tensor fields; §3.1.1-3.1.3 printed pp. 91-99 (PDF pp. 98-106) on the metric, Lorentzian manifolds and the vector-covector isomorphism; §4.5 printed pp. 189-193 (PDF pp. 196-200) on the energy-momentum tensor of matter; §4.5.7 printed pp. 194-198 (PDF pp. 201-205) on energy conditions; natural units printed p. 144 (PDF p. 151).

contents.name: §3.1.1-3.1.2 Riemannian and Lorentzian manifolds: metric, orthonormal basis at a point, past and future lightcones (printed pp. 92-94, PDF pp. 99-101)
contents.support: The notes take a manifold with one negative diagonal metric entry, an orthonormal basis at each point and past/future lightcones whose directions vary smoothly; the definition records the same data as a smooth metric of inertia (3,1,0) and a smooth timelike field.

contents.name: §3.1.3 the vector-covector isomorphism and lengths from the metric (printed pp. 94-96, PDF pp. 101-103)
contents.support: Raising and lowering with the metric is presented as the canonical isomorphism between tangent and cotangent spaces, which is exactly the flat map and its inverse in the definition.

contents.name: §2.3.3 tensors and tensor fields (printed pp. 72-75, PDF pp. 79-82)
contents.support: Tensor fields are smooth multilinear component families with the Jacobian transformation; the definition restricts the rank and proves the chart-independence of smoothness.

contents.name: §3.2 connections and curvature: covariant derivative, Christoffel symbols (printed pp. 100-107, PDF pp. 107-114)
contents.reason: The connection construction, its Christoffel symbols and the curvature of the Levi-Civita connection are developed on the connections and curvature pages; this page fixes only compatibility and torsion freedom.

contents.name: §4.5 the energy-momentum tensor of matter: dust, perfect fluids (printed pp. 189-193, PDF pp. 196-200)
contents.support: The matter examples show that the stress-energy tensor is supplied by the model; the definition here fixes only the tensor slot, its smoothness, symmetry and unit reading and defers the branches.

contents.name: §4.5.7 energy conditions: weak, strong, null and dominant (printed pp. 194-198, PDF pp. 201-205)
contents.support: All four measured-form inequalities are defined, together with the warning that matter violating most of them is easy to find; the definition keeps the exact pointwise forms as optional model assumptions.

contents.name: §4.5.7 perfect-fluid evaluation of the weak and strong conditions (rho >= 0, P >= -rho, P >= -rho/3) (printed pp. 194-196, PDF pp. 201-203)
contents.reason: The evaluation of the energy conditions on a perfect fluid requires the fluid stress-energy branch, which is constructed on the Einstein-and-matter page.

contents.name: natural units and dimensions of G (printed p. 144, PDF p. 151)
contents.support: The notes discuss setting c = 1 and G = 1 and track dimensions of G; the unit item records the natural-unit shorthand and the rule that c and G_N be restored explicitly.

sources.title: J. M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed., Graduate Texts in Mathematics 218, 726 PDF pages (author-hosted copy)
sources.locator: Ch. 1 'Smooth Manifolds' printed pp. 1-31: topological manifolds, smooth structures, examples; Ch. 3 'Tangent Vectors' printed pp. 50-74: tangent vectors as derivations, the differential, computations in coordinates, the tangent bundle; Ch. 12 'Tensors' printed pp. 304-326, especially 'Tensors and Tensor Fields on Manifolds' p. 316; Ch. 13 'Riemannian Metrics' printed pp. 327-347, especially 'The Tangent-Cotangent Isomorphism' p. 341 and 'Pseudo-Riemannian Metrics' p. 343.

contents.name: Ch. 1 'Topological Manifolds' and 'Smooth Structures' (printed pp. 1-16)
contents.support: The smooth-manifold interface consumed here is the published library definition, whose topological and atlas conventions follow the same treatment.

contents.name: Ch. 3 'Tangent Vectors' and 'Computations in Coordinates' (printed pp. 51-64)
contents.support: Tangent vectors as derivations and their coordinate basis are the published interfaces used by the definition of smooth tensor fields.

contents.name: Ch. 12 'Tensors and Tensor Fields on Manifolds' (printed pp. 316-326)
contents.support: Smooth tensor fields are defined by smooth component functions in charts with the multilinear transformation law; the definition specializes to (0,2) fields and proves chart-independence of smoothness.

contents.name: Ch. 13 'The Tangent-Cotangent Isomorphism' and 'Pseudo-Riemannian Metrics' (printed pp. 341-347)
contents.support: The isomorphism between tangent and cotangent spaces induced by a nondegenerate metric, and the pseudo-Riemannian signature conventions, are exactly the pointwise content of the musical isomorphisms and the Lorentzian signature hypothesis.

contents.name: Ch. 13 'Riemannian Manifolds' (printed pp. 327-341)
contents.reason: The positive-definite Riemannian theory is not the arena of this page; the framework's metric is Lorentzian and the library's Riemannian Levi-Civita items are deliberately not consumed for indefinite metrics.
